candidate.name: LOW_OCCURRENCE_DAVIS_PUTNAM_KERNEL
candidate.rule: While there exists a variable v with total occurrence degree d(v)<=3, eliminate v exactly by Davis-Putnam resolution. Use a fixed deterministic tie-break, e.g. lexicographically first variable.
candidate.rank: number of remaining variables while the rule applies

single_step_bound.let: p=number of positive occurrences of v, q=number of negative occurrences, d=p+q<=3
single_step_bound.consequence: The clause count cannot increase; for d>=1 it decreases by at least d-p*q, which is at least 1 for d<=3, before additional tautology/subsumption deletions.
single_step_bound.work: Polynomial in the current CNF size.
single_step_bound.trajectory: At most n variable eliminations, with nonincreasing clause count, hence polynomial live-state and polynomial charged work for this reduction phase.

hard_frontier.published_boundary: 3-SAT remains NP-complete under exact four-occurrence restrictions; stronger results give exact-3-literal monotone families with every variable occurring exactly four times under balanced or related sign restrictions.
hard_frontier.source: Andreas Darmann and Janosch Döcker, On simplified NP-complete variants of Monotone 3-Sat, Discrete Applied Mathematics 292 (2021), 45-58, DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2020.12.010; together with the classical Tovey bounded-occurrence boundary.
hard_frontier.effect: There are arbitrarily large NP-hard 3-SAT instances on which every variable has occurrence degree 4, so the low-occurrence DP rule has no legal first move.
hard_frontier.scope: NP-hardness of the fixed-point class does not prove P!=NP. It proves only that this reduction rule is not a universal exact descent mechanism unless the remaining degree-4 core is solved by an additional theorem.

next_admissible_math.question: Can one define one exact polynomial rule for the min-occurrence-degree>=4 residual core that either strictly lowers a global polynomial rank or transforms it into a polynomially recognizable terminal class, without reintroducing branching, proof search, or exponential state?
